chunks: on hankering after whims, mutual quarrelling, deviation, and dissension.
So, whoever hankers after whims does not incline towards right;
whoever quarrels much on account of ignorance remains permanently blinded from the right;
whoever deviates, for him good becomes evil and evil becomes good and he remains intoxicated with misguidance;
and whoever makes a breach, his path becomes difficult, his affairs become complicated and his way of escape becomes narrow.

key_terms.التَّعَمُّقِ: Hankering after whims or deep attachment to desires
key_terms.الزَّيْغِ: Deviation from the truth or straight path

ai.seo_question: What are the four pillars of unbelief according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) identifies four spiritual diseases that lead to *kufr*: deep-rooted adherence to whims (*al-ta'muq*), contentiousness born of ignorance (*al-tanazu'*), deviation (*al-zaygh*), and dissension (*al-shiqaq*). These states result in a hardened heart that rejects truth, inverts moral values, and creates insurmountable obstacles in one's spiritual journey. This analysis reflects the Shia emphasis on internal cognitive states as the root of external disbelief.
